scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r12 dummy interfaces lo1, lo2, lo3
Mechanism: r12's four /24 loopbacks live on separate Linux
  interfaces (lo, lo1, lo2, lo3) — that's the workaround for
  FRR eigrpd only advertising one prefix per interface. When
  lo1/lo2/lo3 go down, EIGRP withdraws those three prefixes;
  102.1.1.0/24 (on the real `lo`) stays advertised. R11
  withdraws them upstream into OSPF.
Localization: r12
Root cause: dummy interfaces lo1/lo2/lo3 are down on r12
Fix: `ip link set lo1 up; ip link set lo2 up; ip link set lo3 up`
  on r12
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set lo1 up; ip link set lo2 up; ip link set lo3 up`
  on r12

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on r12: loopback interfaces lo1, lo2, and lo3 — which carry the
addresses 102.1.2.1/24, 102.1.3.1/24, and 102.1.4.1/24 respectively — have
been administratively set to state DOWN (confirmed via `ip addr show` on r12).
Because these are BROADCAST/NOARP-type dummy loopbacks rather than the system
loopback (lo), the Linux kernel does not install connected routes for them when
they are down. As a result, FRR's EIGRP process on r12 cannot match those three
`network` statements against any active interface and does not include
102.1.2.0/24, 102.1.3.0/24, or 102.1.4.0/24 in its EIGRP topology table (all
three are absent from r12's `show ip eigrp topology` output). r12 therefore
stops advertising those three prefixes to its EIGRP neighbor r11. Once r11's
EIGRP hold-timer expires for those entries, r11 removes them from its topology
and withdraws them from its OSPF redistribution, causing r1 to lose those three
OSPF external routes via eth1 (111.1.1.2). 102.1.1.0/24 is unaffected because
its source interface is the always-UP system loopback `lo`. The selective
removal of exactly /2, /3, /4 — but not /1 — is entirely explained by the
administrative DOWN state of lo1, lo2, lo3 on r12 alone.

Root cause: `ip link set lo{1,2,3} down` was executed on r12, disabling the
three dummy loopback interfaces that source those prefixes into EIGRP.

Corrective fix: On r12, run `ip link set lo1 up`, `ip link set lo2 up`, and
`ip link set lo3 up`. This restores the connected routes, EIGRP re-advertises
all four 102.1.x.0/24 prefixes to r11, and r11 redistributes them into OSPF,
restoring the routes in r1's RIB within one EIGRP/OSPF convergence cycle.
